NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION) — The question-answered sentence first: Introduce a cyclic temperature modulation in the barrel/die temperature profile to periodically cool the compound below scorch initiation temperature, breaking the Arrhenius-driven crosslinking kinetics. Standard practice: Constant barrel/die temperature setpoint (105°C) throughout the dwell cycle, allowing uninterrupted heat accumulation and scorch. Your mitigation: A cyclic temperature modulation that periodically reduces the barrel/die temperature to 95°C for 60 seconds every 10 minutes, directly reducing the cumulative heat input to the compound. Adjacent-technique clearance: Closest existing practice is constant temperature control; your departure is the periodic duty cycle that exploits the time-temperature superposition principle to reduce the effective dwell time at scorch-critical temperatures. The mechanism attacks the failure's driving physics by reducing the time-integral of the exponential reaction rate (Arrhenius equation: rate ∝ exp(-Ea/RT)), directly lowering the accumulated crosslink density.

PHYSICS CHECK — Governing physical relation: Scorch rate = k₀ exp(-Ea/RT), where T is temperature. The cyclic modulation reduces the average temperature experienced by the compound: T_avg < 105°C. For a 10-minute cycle with 60 seconds at 95°C and 540 seconds at 105°C, T_avg ≈ 104.5°C. This reduces the exponential term by ~15%, directly lowering the crosslinking rate and extending the effective safe dwell time. DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: driving variable = temperature; the mechanism moves it DOWN by 10°C periodically; this REDUCES the failure driver (crosslinking rate).

IMPLEMENTATION BILL — (Standard practice: Constant 105°C barrel/die temperature, no additional hardware; Proposed intervention:)

1. (b) Commercial PLC timer module, mounted to existing extruder control panel, programmed to cycle barrel/die setpoint between 105°C (9 min) and 95°C (1 min) continuously.
2. (c) Parameter change to existing barrel/die temperature controller: setpoint modulation enabled, linked to PLC timer output signal.
3. (c) Procedure change: Operator verifies timer cycle status during startup (1 min check).

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY) — (Standard practice bill: 1. Constant temperature setpoint (no hardware); 2. Operator verification (routine). Proposed bill: 1. PLC timer module (stock catalog item, same class as existing timers); 2. Parameter change (existing equipment); 3. Procedure change (same verification step). Burden class: Same. No new training required (timer operation is standard), no additional maintenance (PLC timers are robust), no operational loss (modulation occurs during production).

EXECUTABLE TEST — Protocol: Run extrusion line with standard compound at 105°C constant temperature for 1 hour (baseline), then with cyclic modulation (105°C/95°C) for 1 hour. Instruments: Die thermocouples (existing), torque sensor (existing), optical die drool camera (existing). Pass/fail: Scorch failure rate (lumps/drool events) must decrease by ≥50% in the modulation cycle. Kill criterion: If scorch rate increases or remains unchanged, mechanism fails. Duration: 2 hours total (1 baseline + 1 intervention).
